minutes.headline: Town manager says finance-department transition is causing substantial, monthslong operational and financial disruption
minutes.summary: The Select Board heard a Lunenburg Snow Riders equipment gift, ratified three town-hire appointments, and voted to sign a Massachusetts Teachers Association-linked advocacy letter to the state legislature on FY27 school funding over one member's objection about scope and a resident's objection about partisanship. The board worked through special-town-meeting warrant articles (voting recommendations on two planning board articles), heard the town manager describe a difficult and costly finance-department staffing transition and a corrected new-growth figure, and set up scheduling for a pre-town-meeting session and a tri-board meeting with the schools before entering executive session on a non-union personnel matter.

public_comment.topic: objected to the process behind the board's vote withholding the historic commission/APDC merger warrant article and its effect on volunteers and civil discourse; raised whether the town should reimburse volunteers for public records request work

public_comment.stated_role: resident, 275 Cross Road; chair of the Lunenburg Republican Town Committee
public_comment.topic: objected to the board signing on to a Massachusetts Teachers Association-linked letter, calling the MTA a partisan organization and citing its members' reactions to the killing of Charlie Kirk

Ratify the town manager's appointment of Deborah Crowley as administrative assistant of the building department
Ratify the town manager's appointment of Lee Bane as administrative assistant of planning
Sign on to the letter to the governor and legislative delegation regarding FY27 school funding, as amended

Enter executive session under MGL c.30 §21(a)(2) for strategy in preparation for/contract negotiations with a non-union employee, the director of municipal finance/town accountant, and not return to open session
votes.outcome: passed 5-0 (roll call: Mloud yes, Leon yes, Em yes, Moore yes, chair yes)

budget_items.what_was_said: The Lunenburg Snow Riders donated a portable chainsaw for police/fire use; no vote was needed because it falls under the gift-acceptance policy threshold.
The Snow Riders said they have brought over $200,000 in RTP grants to the community over 15 years, an 80/20 grant with roughly $60,000 representing the club's volunteer match.
The town manager reported actual new growth over the estimated $400,000 as approximately $180,000, correcting a rumor it was over a million.
MassDOT agreed to extend the $600,000 small bridge grant through December 31, 2027, so the town will not lose the funding; construction is now expected to run October 2026 to June 2027.

The town manager listed open positions including a new library assistant hire at 19 hours/week, and vacancies for payroll and benefits (36 hrs/week), dietary aide (9 hrs/week), heavy equipment operator, land use director (40 hrs/week) and recreation director (19 hrs/week).
The town manager corrected the earlier new-growth figure, saying it is actually $118,000, not $180,000.
The town manager is working with the finance director toward roughly $150,000 in FY26 budget adjustments, mostly consultant costs and vacation buyouts tied to the finance department transition.
Retiree health insurance came in about $100,000 higher than budgeted; the town manager hopes to absorb it using contingency positions already parked in the active budget.
About $140,000 remains in the health insurance stabilization fund, which the town manager would propose using if the retiree health insurance increase cannot otherwise be absorbed.

The town manager plans to bring the salary reserve transfer funding the first year of the new police contract to town meeting as a matter of tradition, with other salary reserve transfers handled directly at town meeting.

transfers.description: Possible transfer from the health insurance stabilization fund (~$140,000 balance) to cover a retiree health insurance cost increase, if it cannot be absorbed within the active budget
Salary reserve transfer to fund the first year of the police contract, planned to be voted at town meeting
Whether to use the finance committee reserve versus raising and appropriating new growth/state aid for FY26 adjustments; unused finance committee reserve rolls into free cash

decisions.decision: The town meeting warrant article for the PACT (Public Access Cable) transfer will be removed from the special town meeting and moved to the May annual town meeting instead.
Consent calendar for special town meeting will contain only articles 6 (cemetery commission transfer) and the second planning board article (bituminous concrete common driveways).
The board will hold off voting recommendations on article 2 (budget adjustments) and article 3 (payment of prior year bills) until closer to town meeting, pending finance committee input.
Board will tentatively schedule a Select Board meeting for 6 p.m. the Monday before special town meeting to finish remaining article recommendations, and will cancel it if unnecessary.
The next tri-board meeting, with the schools, was tentatively set for Monday, November 24th at 7 p.m., the evening before the tax classification hearing.
Board members will split up review of roughly ten backlogged draft minutes sets prepared by a third-party contractor, signing their names to the ones they take.

what_happened.line: The town manager told the board the finance-department staffing transition is causing months of costly disruption, including roughly an amount as heard in FY26 budget adjustments.
The board voted unanimously to sign an amended letter to the governor and legislature on FY27 school funding, tied to a teachers' union advocacy effort, over objections.
The board recommended approval, 4-1, of the special town meeting article bringing the town into compliance with the MBTA Communities Act.
Votes on the FY26 budget-adjustments and prior-year-bills warrant articles were put off until closer to town meeting, pending finance committee input.
The board ratified three town-manager hires, including a new assistant town accountant, as the finance office rebuilds.

why_it_matters: A disrupted finance office and pending budget adjustments touch the town's accounting capacity heading into the November 18 special town meeting.
Signing the FY27 school-funding letter puts the town's name behind a state advocacy position that a board member and a resident said went beyond the board's role.
The MBTA Communities zoning vote and the driveway and cemetery-transfer articles are among the items residents will be asked to vote on at town meeting.
watch_next: Tri-board meeting with the school committee, tentatively November 24

reconciliation.what: Our minutes against the minutes the town published. caption_error = the same fact the captions rendered badly, resolved by the official reading shown beside the as-heard one; discrepancy = a substantive difference, flagged and not resolved. Neither record is treated as the referee.
reconciliation.summary: The two records agree closely on outcomes: every vote total (5-0-0, 5-0-0, 5-0-0, 4-1-0, 5-0-0) and every dollar figure in ours lines up with the official text, and most differences are captions mishearing names or terms (Thibodeau, Bain, McLeod, Lehtinen, Emkey, "Flat Hill" for "Flatrock," "PEG" for "PACT," and Fire Chief Sullivan for "Chief Sully"). The handful of real discrepancies worth checking are: whether the FY27 school-funding letter motion said "as amended" or "as presented," an unexplained $60,000 RTP figure with no official counterpart, whether the finance committee reserve was framed as an open question or a Town Manager recommendation against using it, and whether the person who accepted the Snow Riders gift was the police chief (as heard) or the fire chief (per official minutes).
